what_happened.line: The School Building Committee held its third public forum on a new grade 6-12 middle-high school beside the current high school; no votes were taken.
The committee said the Board of Selectmen decided this week to finance the project over a 30-year term, after a survey in which about two-thirds preferred it.
The presentation covered the total project budget, the maximum state grant and the local share, with annual cost to an average household given as heard.
Presenters said a renovation and addition would not be reimbursed by the state, and that the town would lose committed state funding and need to reopen TC Passios.
A special town meeting was set for January 7th and the debt exclusion ballot vote for Saturday the 11th.

why_it_matters: The plan would be paid for through a debt exclusion, which adds to property tax bills for the length of the borrowing, so residents will be asked to vote on it at town meeting and at the ballot.
The state share applies only to the option the committee prefers, so the choice between building new and renovating changes both the local cost and whether other schools stay open.

The committee appointed three members to the selection committee that will pre-qualify construction managers at risk.

Space built beyond MSBA-eligible size and material choices both affect the local cost, which voters would later be asked to approve.
